projects.name: Wanderlens
projects.tagline: MCA capstone: photo spots by travellers, for travellers
projects.summary: A social discovery app for travellers and photographers. Real people post geo-tagged photo spots with tips, and you can meet others heading to the same place. Community comes first; AI only helps.

story.problem: Most travel apps put an AI concierge at the centre and treat the people as an afterthought. Photographers end up trading spot tips in DMs and group chats.
story.idea: A crowdsourced photo-spot map where nothing is AI-generated, a connection layer to meet travellers by destination and dates, and lightweight AI that only works with the community's real spots.
story.solution: A React Native app with a spot feed and map, multi-photo geo-tagged posts with camera settings, mutual connections, trip matching, real-time chat, a geo-tag camera with photo styles, and an AI photo-trail planner.
story.learned: Geo data with PostGIS, real-time features with Supabase, privacy by design (photos are re-encoded without hidden GPS data), and why place names need to come from the person, not the phone's geocoder, especially in Arunachal.

features: Spot feed: For you, Nearby, Most liked

projects.name: PinchPop
projects.tagline: A photobooth you control with your hands
projects.summary: A gesture-controlled photobooth game. Frame a shot with your fingers, pinch to capture, solve your own photo as a 3×3 puzzle, and keep it as a polaroid. The web version is live; it's growing into a web + mobile platform.

story.problem: Photobooths are all buttons and touchscreens. Taking the photo is the least fun part.
story.idea: Make the camera itself the game controller: hand gestures to frame, capture and play.
story.solution: Real-time hand tracking in the browser with MediaPipe: frame with index fingers, pinch to capture, drag puzzle pieces with a pinch, then the solved puzzle shatters into a polaroid you can save.
story.learned: Computer vision on the web, turning noisy hand landmarks into reliable gestures, Canvas rendering, and Web Audio for feedback.

projects.name: AlgoVisualizer Pro
projects.summary: An interactive DSA learning tool: step-by-step animations of five sorting algorithms with live comparison, swap and timing stats, plus a side-by-side mode that scores algorithms on real performance.

story.problem: Big-O tables are easy to memorise and hard to feel. Watching an algorithm work makes it click.
story.idea: Animate the algorithms and measure them live, so theory and real numbers sit side by side.
story.solution: Bubble, Selection, Insertion, Merge and Quick Sort with speed control and custom input, live counters, and a comparison mode with theoretical and actual-results views.
story.learned: Modelling algorithms as animation steps, state management with Zustand, and smooth motion with Framer Motion.

projects.name: DevBlog
projects.tagline: A Medium-style home for developer writing
projects.summary: A full-stack MERN blogging platform inspired by Medium and Dev.to. Write rich posts, then get likes, bookmarks, nested comments and followers. Started during my EDXcellence internship and kept growing.

story.problem: Todo lists and notes apps teach CRUD in isolation. I wanted to build something real and complete, where every piece has to connect.
story.idea: A blogging platform has it all: many users with roles, a content editor, a social layer and real security concerns.
story.solution: JWT auth with email verification and password reset, a Quill editor with cover images, drafts, scheduled posts and series, plus likes, bookmarks, nested comments, follows, notifications, author analytics, admin moderation, RSS and a sitemap. It installs as a PWA.
story.learned: How a whole web app fits together and why each choice is made: sanitising HTML on both sides, rate limiting, blocking NoSQL injection, and testing the API with Jest and Supertest against an in-memory MongoDB.

features: PWA with light, dark & sepia themes

projects.name: TripWise
projects.summary: An AI-powered travel planner. Tell it where, when, your budget and your vibe, and it builds a day-by-day itinerary with costs, local tips and a packing list, all running on free tiers.

story.problem: Planning a trip in India means a dozen tabs, and generic AI plans ignore budget, season and how you actually like to travel.
story.idea: Grow SafarNama's itinerary idea into its own product: real AI plans shaped by budget, crew and vibe, wrapped in a design that feels like India's many landscapes.
story.solution: A React + TypeScript site over an Express API: a planner wizard, AI itineraries that appear day by day (Gemini with Groq as fallback, every answer validated), PDF and share links, a travel passport with trip stamps, and friends.
story.learned: Working with LLM APIs reliably (fallbacks, validation, caching, daily limits), designing around free-tier limits, and building a big visual system: seven living Indian landscapes drawn in the browser.

projects.name: SafarNama
projects.summary: SafarNama ("travelogue" in Hindi) is a full-stack platform for exploring India responsibly: find eco-friendly destinations, plan a trip day by day, and share it with SafarGram, a built-in traveller community. A team project; I worked on both the frontend and the backend.

award.title: Special Jury Award, Most Innovative Project
award.detail: ₹10,000 scholarship from the AEC Class 88′ Foundation

story.problem: Travel information is scattered across blogs, reels and random forums, and very little of it nudges people to travel responsibly or to look beyond the usual tourist spots.
story.idea: One traveller-first place that mixes discovery, eco-tourism and community, so planning a trip and caring about the place happen together. It grew out of my own solo trips.
story.solution: A MERN app with a real-time layer: eco-friendly destinations on an interactive map with weather, permits and best-time-to-visit; a rule-based itinerary planner that builds a day-by-day route; SafarGram with posts, 24-hour stories, chat and live notifications over Socket.IO; a community forum, events and eco-guides; and an admin area for moderation.
story.learned: Building a large full-stack app with a team, real-time features with Socket.IO, security basics (hashed passwords, rate limiting, account lockout), testing an API against an in-memory database, and product thinking around a real problem.

projects.name: WanderLink
projects.tagline: Messaging and trip planning for explorers
projects.summary: A traveller-focused Android app that combines messaging, trip planning and social networking. The best travel tips come from people who were just there. (Private repo for now.)

story.problem: On the road, the most useful information comes from other travellers, but there is no easy way to find and talk to them.
story.idea: An app where travellers can meet around places and trips, from one-to-one chats to open communities, and plan trips together.
story.solution: A native Android app with traveller messaging (one-to-one, groups, communities, chat requests), trip planning and a social feed for discovering and sharing travel spots.
story.learned: Native Android with Java and XML layouts, and designing chat features and data models before writing code.
